sections.t: Troubleshooting: L1 (base image) Docker build failures
sections.x:
This guide covers failures in **L1**, the foundational base image layer of Flisk's Docker image stack. It explains what L1 builds, how it relates to the rest of the L1–L4 stack, and how to diagnose and fix the errors you see when L1 fails to build or is missing.

All errors shown on this page were reproduced on a developer workstation running macOS with Docker Desktop.

---

sections.t: Troubleshooting: L1 (base image) Docker build failures
sections.h: What L1 is in plain words
sections.x:
Flisk uses a four-tier layered Docker architecture (L1–L4) to make local image builds fast and cache-friendly across multiple microservices:

| Layer | Name | Purpose | What it contains | Defined in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **L1** | **Base OS & Runtime** | Foundational OS & runtime environment | Alpine Linux base, Bun runtime (`oven/bun:1.3.11-alpine`), essential utilities (`curl`, `bash`, `openssl`, `ca-certificates`, `tzdata`), `app` system user/group, and runtime env vars (`NODE_ENV`, `BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR`). | `l1_base_layers.star` |
| **L2** | Dependencies | Package resolver & module cache | Base layer + common dependencies + pre-warmed `/cache/bun` directory. | `l2_dependency_layers.star` |
| **L3** | Builder | Compilation & asset building | Service compilation, Prisma CLI, frontend bundler, and production pruning. | `l3_builder_layers.star` |
| **L4** | Runtime | Final production/dev container | Lean runtime (Bun for backends, Nginx or Bun static for frontends, migrator). | `l4_runtime_layers.star` |

L1 is the root of the entire stack. Every generated service Dockerfile (`.autogenerated/Dockerfile.*.autogenerated`) and all subsequent golden layers (L2, L3, L4) inherit from L1. If L1 fails to build or is missing from local Docker storage, downstream builds cannot start.

sections.t: Troubleshooting: L2 (dependency layer) Docker build failures
sections.x:
This guide covers failures in **L2**, the dependency resolution and package caching layer of Flisk's Docker image stack. It explains what L2 caches, how dependency manifest inputs and `CACHE_BUSTER` control cache invalidation, and how to diagnose and resolve errors when package installation fails or cache invalidation does not behave as expected.

Outputs on this page were captured on a developer workstation running macOS with Docker Desktop 29.8.2 and Bun 1.3.11. In Case 3A, the symptom, the build-toolchain fix and the `ldd` check were run; the `gcompat` fix and the glibc `Exec format error` variant were not. Package counts, step numbers, durations and timestamps vary by project and machine.

---

sections.t: Troubleshooting: L2 (dependency layer) Docker build failures
sections.h: What L2 is in plain words
sections.x:
In Flisk's four-tier Docker image hierarchy (L1–L4), **L2** is the dependency layer:

| Layer | Name | Purpose | What it contains | Defined in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **L1** | Base OS & Runtime | Foundational OS & runtime | Alpine Linux, Bun runtime (`oven/bun:1.3.11-alpine`), essential utilities (`curl`, `bash`, `openssl`), and system user `app`. | `l1_base_layers.star` |
| **L2** | **Dependencies** | **Package resolver & module cache** | **Installed `node_modules/`, workspace hoisted packages (`.bun`), and package manager cache mounts (`/cache/bun`).** | `l2_dependency_layers.star` |
| **L3** | Builder | Compilation & asset building | Service compilation, Prisma CLI, frontend bundler, and production pruning. | `l3_builder_layers.star` |
| **L4** | Runtime | Final production/dev container | Lean runtime (Bun for backends, Nginx or Bun static for frontends, migrator). | `l4_runtime_layers.star` |

sections.t: Troubleshooting: L2 (dependency layer) Docker build failures
sections.x:
L2 isolates slow, network-bound package downloads and disk-heavy dependency trees (`node_modules`) from fast application code changes. Specifically, L2 caches:
1. **Per-service `node_modules/`:** The resolved package directory under `/app//node_modules`.
2. **Monorepo / hoisted modules:** The shared hoisted directory `/app/node_modules/.bun` used by Bun's isolated linker.
3. **Download cache:** Pre-warmed package tarballs stored in `/cache/bun` (via Docker BuildKit cache mounts: `--mount=type=cache,target=/cache/bun,sharing=shared`).

sections.t: Troubleshooting: L2 (dependency layer) Docker build failures
sections.h: How L2 layer caching and invalidation works
sections.x:
Docker builds use a content-addressable cache. Each instruction in a Dockerfile creates a layer keyed on the hash of the instruction and its inputs:

```text
[L1: Base Image] (oven/bun:1.3.11-alpine)
       ↓
[L2: ARG CACHE_BUSTER]               /node_modules` and `/app/node_modules/.bun` from L2 via `COPY --link --from=l2_deps_manifest`. Because L2's files changed, L3 rebuilds, and finally L4 rebuilds.
4. **Why this design is intentional:** When you edit your application source code (e.g. `src/index.ts`), the manifest files and `CACHE_BUSTER` remain untouched. Docker completely skips L1 and L2, reusing the cached `node_modules` layer in under a second.

sections.t: Troubleshooting: L2 (dependency layer) Docker build failures
sections.h: Where L2 is generated and configured
sections.x:
- **Service Dockerfile generation:** `l2_dependency_layers.star` defines `L2_generate_dependency_manifest`, emitting stage `l2_deps_manifest`:
  ```dockerfile
  # ---- L2: dependency_manifest ----
  FROM -l2:latest AS l2_deps_manifest
  WORKDIR /app

  ARG CACHE_BUSTER=2026-06-25-v1
  RUN echo "Cache buster: ${CACHE_BUSTER}"

  COPY package.json ./package.json
  COPY /.autogenerated/npmrc.docker /app/.npmrc
  COPY /.autogenerated/bunfig.docker.toml /app/.bunfig.toml

  WORKDIR /app/
  COPY /package.json ./package.json
  COPY /.autogenerated/npmrc.docker .npmrc
  COPY /.autogenerated/bunfig.docker.toml .bunfig.toml

  COPY shared-platform-engineering/docker-templates/install-deps.sh /usr/local/bin/install-deps.sh
  RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/cache/bun,sharing=shared \
      chmod +x /usr/local/bin/install-deps.sh && \
      /usr/local/bin/install-deps.sh
  RUN mkdir -p /app/node_modules/.bun
  ```

sections.t: Troubleshooting: L2 (dependency layer) Docker build failures
sections.h: 1. The lockfile is missing or out of date, so the frozen install fails
sections.x:
When dependency verification runs in CI or pre-commit checks with frozen lockfile enforcement enabled, the package manager verifies that the lockfile strictly matches `package.json`. If a dependency was modified in `package.json` without updating the lockfile, the frozen install fails.

> **Note on L2 installer vs host/CI checks:** Flisk's generated L2 build runner (`install-deps.sh`) executes `bun install --force` and does **not** pass `--frozen-lockfile`. The frozen lockfile failures documented below occur during host-level verification, CI workflows (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`), or custom production Dockerfiles that enforce strict lockfile immutability, rather than during standard `flisk up` image builds.

#### Case 1A: Out-of-date lockfile in Bun (`bun install --frozen-lockfile`)

This is a standalone diagnostic. The generated L2 build runs `install-deps.sh`, which executes `bun install --force` without `--frozen-lockfile`, so this error is not the install command that a `flisk up` image build runs.

**Symptom:**
```text
bun install v1.3.11 (af24e281)
Resolving dependencies
Resolved, downloaded and extracted [16]
error: lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen
note: try re-running without --frozen-lockfile and commit the updated lockfile
```
The command terminates with exit code 1.

- **Cause:** `package.json` contains a new, updated, or removed dependency, but `bun.loc

sections.h: 2. A dependency change does not invalidate the cache when it should
sections.x:
#### Symptom:
You updated a dependency (such as publishing a bugfix to a local workspace package, bumping an internal library in Verdaccio, or changing a dependency on disk), but when running `flisk up` or building the container, Docker outputs (shown with `docker build --progress=plain`; step numbers come from one example service and vary):
```text
#17 [l2_deps_manifest  4/13] COPY package.json ./package.json
#17 CACHED
...
#22 [l2_deps_manifest 12/13] RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/cache/bun,sharing=shared chmod +x /usr/local/bin/install-deps.sh && ...
#22 CACHED

1. **Manifest files unchanged:** Docker computes cache keys from the checksums of files named in `COPY` instructions. In `L2_generate_dependency_manifest`, the copied files are:
   - `package.json` (workspace root and service directory)
   - `.npmrc` (`.autogenerated/npmrc.docker`)
   - `.bunfig.toml` (`.autogenerated/bunfig.docker.toml`)

sections.h: 3. The install works on the host but fails inside the image
sections.x:

sections.t: Troubleshooting: L2 (dependency layer) Docker build failures
sections.h: 4. The registry fails for a version published minutes ago
sections.x:
#### Symptom:

```text
→ error: GET https://registry.npmjs.org/rollup/-/rollup-4.67.3.tgz - 404
```

#### Cause:

A new release is listed in the package metadata a few minutes before the registry's CDN serves its tarball. An install that resolves the newest version in that window (any range such as `^4.0.0`) gets a 404 for a version that exists.

#### What the installer does:

- It skips versions published in the last day (`bun install --minimum-release-age=86400`), so a range resolves to the newest release that is at least a day old.
- When a dependency pins a version newer than that (`"rollup": "4.67.3"`), it installs again without the minimum age.
- It retries a tarball 404, a 408, 429 or 5xx answer, a dropped connection, or a stalled install, up to three attempts, waiting 15 s and then 30 s.
- A 404 for package metadata (a package that does not exist) fails at once.
- When the attempts run out on a registry error, the build log says so and suggests running `flisk up` again in a few minutes.

Generated images use these defaults. A custom Dockerfile that runs `install-deps.sh` can set `FLISK_MIN_RELEASE_AGE_SECONDS` (seconds, `0` turns the minimum off), `FLISK_INSTALL_ATTEMPTS` (default `3`) and `FLISK_INSTALL_RETRY_DELAY` (seconds, multiplied by the attempt number; default `15`) in the environment of that `RUN` step.

- **Reproduced:** the output below was captured by running Flisk 1.3.86 (`origin/main` at the time of writing) in a scratch project on macOS. The scratch project's directory is shown as ``. `flisk up` was **not** run for this page, so nothing here was observed while Docker was starting containers.
- **Simulated:** produced by running the real `flisk` against a stand-in for Docker (a small wrapper that makes `docker` fail the way the entry describes). The message and fix are Flisk's own; the Docker failure itself was not real.

sections.h: Required secrets: secret X has no value
sections.x:
```text
$ flisk up --dry-run
❌ 1 required secret without a value:
    services/main/api/service.json: secret SECRET_KEY has no value
   Fix: Add NAME=value to .env (it is gitignored), or export it in the environment, or move it to "optional"
```

- **Cause:** the service lists `SECRET_KEY` in `secrets.required`, and neither the env file of the run (the project `.env`, or the one chosen with `--env-file`) nor the environment has a non-empty value for it. Compose refuses to interpolate such a name, which used to fail the whole Tiltfile and stop every service.
- **Fix:** put `SECRET_KEY=...` in `.env`, export it, or list it under `secrets.optional` if the service can run without it. With `FLISK_SECRET_PROVIDER=infisical` the check is skipped and Infisical supplies the names.
- **Defined in:** `service-config-checks.ts` (`checkRequiredSecrets`), run by the `flisk up` gate, dry run included.
- **Checked:** reproduced by the Docker chaos tier (`secrets=required, no value`) and covered by `service-config-checks.test.ts`.

sections.h: flisk X is older than the Y this project requires (minFliskVersion)
sections.x:
```text
$ flisk up shop --dry-run        # same text from flisk up and flisk doctor
flisk 1.3.86 is older than the 9.9.9 this project requires (minFliskVersion)
Run: flisk upgrade
```

With `"minFliskVersion": "abc"` in `.flisk/project.json`:

```text
.flisk/project.json minFliskVersion "abc" is not a version like "1.3.80"
Set minFliskVersion to a MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH string, for example "1.3.80".
```

- **Cause:** the repository pins a minimum CLI version and yours is older, or the pin is not `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. Both stop `flisk up` with exit code 1, before Docker or Tilt are touched.
- **Fix:** `flisk upgrade`, or install a specific version; see upgrading. `flisk up --ignore-version` skips the check, which is only sensible when the pin is stale.
- **Defined in:** `flisk-version.ts`.
- **Checked:** reproduced with a scratch `minFliskVersion` of `9.9.9` and `abc`.

sections.h: Docker build cache exceeds 10 GB threshold
sections.x:
```text
⚠ 11.82GB across 780 entries: Docker build cache exceeds 10 GB threshold. Cache is shared across all projects on this machine
ℹ Fix: Prune old build cache: flisk down --prune-cache (or docker builder prune --filter until=24h). Note: this affects other projects on this machine.
```

- **Cause:** Starting stacks builds golden base image layers and mounts package caches (`RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/cache/bun`) so builds take seconds instead of minutes. Over time, Docker build cache grows by several gigabytes. Because Docker build cache is daemon-global, it is shared across all projects on the machine.
- **Fix:** Run `flisk down --prune-cache` when stopping your stack. It safely prunes cache older than 24 hours (`docker builder prune -f --filter until=24h`), preserving warm cache for recent builds while reclaiming gigabytes of disk space. Customize the retention window with `--cache-until ` (e.g. `flisk down --prune-cache --cache-until 7d`). In interactive terminals, it prompts for confirmation; pass `-y` / `--yes` in scripts. Or run `flisk doctor --fix` when host disk space is low (< 10 GB).
- **Checked:** tested with mocked `docker system df` and unit tests pinning the 10 GB threshold and guarded pruning.

sections.h: Docker cannot create another network: all predefined address pools are in use
sections.x:
```text
✗ Docker cannot create another network: all predefined address pools are in use. Each Flisk project needs several
ℹ Fix: Run flisk doctor --fix --scope=machine: it removes unused networks of every Flisk project and keeps the ones in use. Or run flisk down --prune-networks in each project you are not using
```

- **Cause:** Docker's default address pools are used up. Each Flisk project creates several networks and keeps them after `flisk down`. Docker's own error text is `all predefined address pools have been fully subnetted`; doctor matches `address pools`.
- **Fix:** run `flisk doctor --fix --scope=machine`. It lists every unused network that belongs to a Flisk project (each with its owner), skips any network with a container attached, and asks before it removes them; add `--dry-run` to only list them. Alternatives: `flisk down --prune-networks` in each project you no longer use, or `docker network prune`, which removes every unused network on that Docker daemon, whoever created it. `--prune-networks` was added in #585.
- **If you skip doctor:** since #589, the `init-networks` resource in Tilt fails with `Failed to create Docker network : ` and exits 1. Before it, the failure was swallowed (the command ended `|| true`), `init-networks` reported success, and the later failure was `network ... declared as external, but could not be found`, which is what byo.md and the m

sections.x:
```text
⚠ Potential secret-looking values detected in public environment variables: NEXT_PUBLIC_API_KEY (.env)
ℹ Fix: Move secrets to server-side variables or API routes. Public variables (NEXT_PUBLIC_*, VITE_*) are embedded into client bundles.
```

- **Cause:** a client-accessible variable prefixed with `NEXT_PUBLIC_` (Next.js) or `VITE_` (Vite) holds a value that matches high-confidence credential signatures (for example Stripe secret keys `sk_live_`, AWS credentials `AKIA`, GitHub tokens `ghp_`, OpenAI keys `sk-proj-`, Slack tokens `xoxb-`, Google API keys `AIza`, private keys, JWTs, or embedded URL credentials). The bundler inlines these values directly into the browser-facing JavaScript bundle where any visitor can inspect them.
- **Warning-only:** this check is an informational warning (`⚠`) by default, so it does not fail `flisk doctor` or block local developer workflows. When run with `flisk doctor --strict`, it is treated as a blocking failure.
- **Redaction:** `flisk doctor` outputs only the variable name and the relative file path. Secret values are never printed in diagnostic messages, error output, JSON envelopes, or logs.
- **Publishable keys allowed:** known public-by-design identifiers, such as Stripe publishable keys (`pk_live_`, `pk_test_`) and common placeholders (`sk_test_x`), are recognized and permitted.
- **Fix:** rotate any leaked credential immediately

- **Cause:** a local-process service declares `"toolchain": "node@24"` (or `python@3.12`, ...) in its `service.json`, and the program on `PATH` is another version, is missing, or did not report a version. `flisk up` stops before starting anything; `flisk doctor` fails the **Service toolchains** check.

sections.h: container is running, but its health check is failing, and the probe says curl: not found
sections.x:
```text
❌ flisk up failed:
  lychee-facial-recognition: container is running, but its health check is failing
$ docker inspect --format '{{range .State.Health.Log}}[{{.ExitCode}}] {{.Output}}{{end}}' 
[127] /bin/sh: 1: curl: not found      (exec form: [-1] OCI runtime exec failed: ... executable file not found in $PATH)
```

- **Cause:** the image's health command (often imported from a Compose `healthcheck`) does not exist in the image, so the probe never runs while the app itself serves. Docker records that as exit 127 (or 126, not executable) for a shell-form check, and as exit -1 with `OCI runtime exec failed ... executable file not found` for the exec form (`test: [CMD, curl, ...]`) that Flisk writes. Flisk waits on Docker's health status, so `flisk up` used to fail on it.
- **What Flisk does now:** when the container is running and every recorded probe shows its command never ran, `flisk up` and the `-healthy` wait proceed with a warning instead of failing. The evidence is in the probe's own result: exit -1 with `OCI runtime exec failed` (exec form), exit 127 with `not found` in the output, or exit 126 with `permission denied` and the like (shell form). An exit code alone is not enough, since a script that did run can exit 127. Docker keeps only the last five probes, so for the shell form the whole failing streak must be inside that log; an older real failure that scrolle

sections.h: No available host port in ... for ...
sections.x:
```text
No available host port in 15432-15532 for postgres. Set FLISK_POSTGRES_PORT to a free port and retry.
```

- **Cause:** every candidate port for that service is taken, usually because many projects are running. HTTP, HTTPS and Postgres each have a range of 101 ports (8080-8180, 8443-8543 and 15432-15532). Every project takes a Postgres port from its range, so at most 101 projects fit with the defaults, fewer if other programs hold ports in it. HTTP and HTTPS try 80 and 443 first and take a port from their range only when that port is not usable, so the first project does not use up a range port. The message names the first service whose candidates run out. That is `postgres` when 80 and 443 are both usable, `ingressHttp` when 80 is not (it is taken, or on Linux and WSL2 a non-root user cannot check it), and `ingressHttps` when only 443 is not.
- **Fix:** stop projects you no longer need with `flisk down`, or set the variable the message names for this project: `FLISK_HTTP_PORT` for `ingressHttp`, `FLISK_HTTPS_PORT` for `ingressHttps`, `FLISK_POSTGRES_PORT` for `postgres`. The ranges cannot be changed. An override is used as-is: if that port is taken, Flisk reports it instead of picking another.
- **Defined in:** `host-port-plan.ts`.

sections.x:

Networks created by `init-networks` are kept after `flisk down` unless you pass it.

sections.t: Troubleshooting: flisk and Tilt messages and what to do about them
sections.h: docker images lists every service twice (:dev and :tilt-<hash>), and old builds fill the disk
sections.x:
```text
__   dev                ddbc536add42
__   tilt-ddbc536add42  ddbc536add42
```

- **Cause:** Tilt builds each image as `:tilt-`, tags it with the `:dev` name the compose service uses, and from then on uses only `:dev`. The `tilt-*` tag stays. Both tags are one image, so the pair costs no space, but after a rebuild the previous build keeps its own `tilt-*` tag, so a full old image per service stays on disk until Tilt's own prune.
- **Fix:** the `tilt-image-tags` resource (label `infra.docker`) removes this project's `tilt-*` tags when `flisk up` starts and each time a build is tagged `:dev`: the tag on the current image, and old builds. An old build still used by the container compose is replacing goes once that container is removed. A newer build that Tilt has not tagged `:dev` yet is left alone. To keep the tags, run `FLISK_KEEP_TILT_TAGS=1 flisk up`. On a version without it, `docker image rm :tilt-` removes a tag by hand; it never deletes an image another tag still names.
- **Defined in:** `tilt_image_tags.star`, registered by `load_all_infrastructure` in `infra-loader.star`.

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| `1`–`5` | Jump to Overview, Resources, Events, Files, Config |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Next / previous tab |
| `↑`/`↓` or `j`/`k` | Move the highlight |

- `--no-animations`: disable animations (static spinner text).

- `NO_COLOR` is set, even to an empty value, or

sections.t: Upgrading Flisk and keeping a team on one version
sections.h: Set a minimum version for the repo
sections.x:
Add `minFliskVersion` to `.flisk/project.json` and commit it:

```json
{ "minFliskVersion": "1.3.80" }
```

`flisk doctor` and `flisk up` then fail on any older CLI, locally and in CI, and say what to run:

```text
flisk 1.3.79 is older than the 1.3.80 this project requires (minFliskVersion)
Run: flisk upgrade
```

- It is a **floor**: newer versions pass. Nothing pins an exact version.
- The value must be `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; anything else fails the check.
- `flisk up` checks it first, before the Docker checks and before Tilt starts, and exits 1 with the two lines above. A malformed value stops it too. A project without `minFliskVersion` is not checked.
- `flisk up --dry-run` runs the same check and exits 1 on a failure, as it does for generated-file drift; nothing is started either way.
- `flisk up --ignore-version` skips the check and prints a warning. Use it only to get past a pin you know is stale; `flisk doctor` still reports it.

The workflow `e2e-platforms-hardware.yml` has two jobs:

- **hosted** runs the suite on `windows-latest` on every pull request that touches the Windows platform code. It is a reference run and a canary on the published release, not the acceptance run.
- **hardware** runs the same suite on a self-hosted Windows 11 AMD64 machine. It only runs when someone dispatches the workflow by hand, so a pull request never executes on a maintainer's machine.

To use it, register a runner on the Windows machine with the labels `self-hosted`, `windows` and `x64`, then dispatch **🪟 Platforms hardware E2E** from the Actions tab. The `release` input pins the release to test; the findings report is uploaded as the artifact `windows-hardware-findings-machine-`.

The design for first-class Windows support asks for a human acceptance run on a real Windows 11 AMD64 machine before any support claim changes (`openspec/changes/flisk-windows-first-class-support/tasks.md`, task 7.3). `flisk up` is not a cluster. It starts Docker containers on your machine through Tilt.

`service.json` is not `values.yaml`. `service.json` describes the local service (ports, stack, health URL). `values.yaml` configures Kubernetes objects (Deployment, Service, Ingress).

Flisk does not replace Helm. Helm remains the templating engine for the cluster. Flisk only templates the machine environment (see scope and non-goals for what differs from production). Keep app-template or the chart you already use for production; Flisk does not install or take over those charts.

```text
Local:   flisk up shop      → containers on the machine, *.localhost
Cluster: helm upgrade …   → Deployment/Service in Kubernetes
```

Flisk: local development for multi-service apps, started with one command.

Flisk is the local development inner loop. It scaffolds services, generates local Dockerfile layers and Tilt configuration, starts local proxy/Postgres services, and lets you choose which local services to run. Helm and your cluster tooling own replicas, readiness/liveness probes, ingress class and hosts, PVCs, node selectors, IRSA, HPA, and other production policy.

These fields are related ideas, not a one-to-one configuration translation. Local startup order, routes, and resource types do not define a cluster release.

`service.json` configures Flisk's machine development loop. Helm `values.yaml` configures chart resources for Kubernetes. Shared concepts such as an image name or port must be deliberately carried across; the files are not equivalent, and Flisk does not generate Helm values.

On Windows, you run Flisk inside the **Ubuntu** app. Ubuntu is a free version of Linux, and WSL2 (Windows Subsystem for Linux) is the part of Windows that runs it, next to your usual Windows apps. You install it once with one command, then type every Flisk command in the Ubuntu app, which is your terminal on Windows.

Why the extra step? Flisk starts your app with Linux tools: Linux containers, Docker and Tilt. Docker Desktop and Tilt both run on Windows, but Flisk's Tilt engine runs POSIX shell commands on the host (see why native Windows cannot start a Docker stack), and Ubuntu on WSL2 provides that environment.

Just want the short version? Set up Windows has three steps. Never written code? Start here. This page has every step in detail, an example app to try, and fixes for common problems.

Which Flisk commands work where. In short: on Windows, use the Ubuntu app for the full Docker stack. Windows on its own ("native Windows") runs apps whose services each declare a `command` (local processes, no Docker), runs `flisk demo`, checks your computer and shows what Flisk would start; it cannot start a Docker stack.

| Platform | `flisk up` | `flisk doctor` | `flisk --version` | `flisk up --dry-run` | Notes |
|----------|------------|----------------|-------------------|----------------------|-------|
| macOS / Linux | ✅ Full runtime | ✅ Full | ✅ | ✅ | Native support |
| **WSL2 Ubuntu** | ✅ Full runtime | ✅ Full | ✅ | ✅ | **Recommended for Windows** |
| Native Windows | ✅ Local processes · ❌ Docker stack | ✅ Inspection only | ✅ | ✅ Inspection only | See below |

**Bottom line**: Run Flisk from **Ubuntu inside WSL2** for the full Docker stack. Native Windows runs `flisk demo` and projects whose services each declare a `command` (without Docker), plus the inspection commands (`flisk --version`, `flisk doctor`, `flisk up --dry-run`); `flisk up` on a Docker project exits with a clear refusal pointing to WSL2.

- Windows 10 22H2+ or Windows 11 (WSL2 requires Windows 10 1903+; 22H2+ recommended for best compatibility)
- WSL2 installed: `wsl --install -d Ubuntu` (or `wsl --install` for default Ubuntu)
- Docker Desktop for Windows with **WSL2 backend** selected
- Admin rights for Docker Desktop installation

In WSL2 Ubuntu with Docker running, this clones the starter, installs dependencies, boots the stack, and opens the frontend. On native Windows (or without Docker) it starts the small two-service demo as local processes instead.

sections.h: Native Windows: what works and what doesn't
sections.x:
| Command | Native Windows | WSL2 Ubuntu |
|---------|----------------|-------------|
| `flisk --version` | ✅ Prints version | ✅ |
| `flisk doctor` | ✅ Inspection checks | ✅ Full checks |
| `flisk up --dry-run` | ✅ Shows what would start | ✅ |
| `flisk up` (services with `command`) | ✅ Local processes | ✅ |
| `flisk up ` (Docker) | ❌ Exits 1 with WSL2 guidance | ✅ Boots stack |
| `flisk demo` | ✅ Small demo, local processes | ✅ Full demo flow |
| `flisk restaurant` and other Docker starters | ❌ Refuses before cloning | ✅ |

**Why?** Docker Desktop (Linux containers) and `tilt.exe` do run on native Windows. The blocker is Flisk's own Tilt engine: its Starlark discovery and build steps run `sh -c`, `find`, `test -f`, `mkdir -p` and `.sh` scripts on the host, which `cmd.exe` and PowerShell do not provide (Windows has its own `find.exe`, but it is not POSIX `find`). The CLI therefore refuses early to avoid partial or confusing state. Local processes need none of that.

If you are on native Windows and see:
```
Landscape startup needs Ubuntu on WSL2. Native Windows runs only services that declare a command, as local processes.
```
→ Open **Ubuntu (WSL2)** and run the commands there.

After setup, run these to confirm readiness:

```sh
# 1. Docker reachable
docker ps

# 2. Tilt installed
tilt version

# 3. Flisk installed
flisk --version

# 4. Doctor passes
flisk doctor

# 5. Config verifies (in a project)
flisk config verify
```

All should succeed without errors. If not, see Troubleshooting.

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| `docker version` fails / "Cannot connect to the Docker daemon" | WSL integration not enabled | Docker Desktop → Settings → Resources → WSL Integration → enable Ubuntu → Apply & Restart → restart Ubuntu |
| `flisk doctor` shows port 80/443/5432 conflict | Another process holds the port | `netstat -ano \| findstr :80` (Windows) or `ss -tlnp \| grep :80` (Ubuntu) → stop the process or set `FLISK_HTTP_PORT` |
| `flisk up` picks port 8080+ instead of 80 | Non-root user cannot bind port 80 on Linux/WSL2 | Expected behavior; use the printed URL with the port. Or run `sudo setcap 'cap_net_bind_service=+ep' $(which docker)` (not recommended) |
| `flisk doctor` warns about `FLISK_BIND_ADDRESS` | Wildcard bind address exposes ports to network | Unset `FLISK_BIND_ADDRESS` to keep ports on `127.0.0.1` |
| `flisk up` fails with "Tilt not found" | Tilt not in PATH | `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tilt-dev/tilt/master/scripts/install.sh \| bash` then restart shell |
| `bun: command not found` | Bun not installed | `curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install \| bash` or install via npm |

| Feature | Status | Notes |
|---------|--------|-------|
| Native Windows `flisk up` (Docker stack) | Not supported | No Linux container runtime; use WSL2. Local-process projects work |
| Docker Desktop without WSL2 backend | Not supported | Hyper-V backend has different networking; use WSL2 backend |
| Windows Containers | Not supported | Flisk generates Linux container configs only |
| ARM64 Windows | Untested | AMD64 only for now |
